title: Closed base restriction of a vanishing topos
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), let $f:X\to S$ be of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $k:T\hookrightarrow S$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $X_T=X\times_ST$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$. Form $E_T=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ using [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. The canonical morphism $E_T\to V_f$ identifies $E_T$ with the inverse image under the second projection $p_2:V_f\to S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ of the closed subtopos $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The morphism $V_{f_T}\to E_T$ induced by $X_T\to X$ and $k$ is an equivalence. Here $V_f,V_{f_T}$ are as in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Its inverse-image equivalence identifies finite-stratification constructibility on $E_T$ with that on $V_{f_T}$, both for sheaves of finite sets and for sheaves of modules over a finite commutative constant ring $\Lambda$: on $E_T$ this means finite constructible locally closed partitions of $X$ and $T$ on whose oriented products the sheaf is locally constant with finite values, as in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf] with sets in place of modules when appropriate. Inverse image to $E_T$ preserves these constructible sheaves. The same assertions apply after replacing $X$ by any closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow X$, with $Z_T=Z\times_ST$.

source.place: Author draft, Lemma 8.3.1, printed p. 18, specialized to the integral morphism T closed in S, together with the rectangular restrictions in Section 8.1 and the proof of Lemma 8.3.3, printed pp. 17–19. The equivalence is the closed-immersion case of 8.3.1, not an ordinary Cartesian product of topoi.

proof.text: Write $U=S\setminus T$ and $U_X=X\times_SU=X\setminus X_T$, and let $u=h_U$ and $u_X=h_{U_X}$ be their subterminal etale sheaves. For any scheme map $e:A\to B$ and etale object $W\to B$, the set-sheaf adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], representable sheaf property [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf], and Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give, naturally in $H$, $\operatorname{Hom}(e^{-1}h_W,H)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_W,e_*H)=H(A\times_BW)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_{A\times_BW},H)$. Thus $e^{-1}h_W\simeq h_{A\times_BW}$. In particular $f^{-1}u\simeq u_X$ and $k^{-1}u=0$, since $T\times_SU$ is empty. The sheaf $h_{\varnothing}$ is initial: Yoneda identifies maps from it to $H$ with $H(\varnothing)$, a singleton by the empty covering of the empty object. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $q:X_T\hookrightarrow X$ is closed. The scheme clause of [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization] identifies $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $(X_T)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with the closed complements of $u$ and $u_X$.

source.place: Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward; the displayed representable calculation is the adjunction and Yoneda argument for small-etale base change.

proof.text: Let $p_1,p_2$ be the projections of $V_f$. The universal property [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] gives $r:E_T\to V_f$ from $X\to X$, $T\to S$ and the structural $2$-arrow. For any topos $\mathcal H$, a morphism $a:\mathcal H\to V_f$ consists of $a_1:\mathcal H\to X_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $a_2:\mathcal H\to S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and $a_2\Rightarrow fa_1$. It factors through $E_T$ precisely when $a_2$ factors through $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. By [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization], the latter is equivalent to $a_2^{-1}u=0$, with unique compatible factorization including $2$-morphisms. Consequently $r$ is the closed complement of $p_2^{-1}u$, hence is exactly the asserted inverse image of $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. This identifies the canonical morphism, not just an abstractly equivalent topos.

source.place: XI Theorem 1.4 and §1.9; closed-complement factorization is Stacks 08LY, lemma-closed-subtopos, through the cited localization statement.

proof.text: For the equivalence, allow an arbitrary additional scheme map $l:Y\to T$; this will also cover the stratum restrictions. Put $P_Y=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ using $kl:Y\to S$, and $Q_Y=(X_T)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{T_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The universal property gives $v_Y:Q_Y\to P_Y$. Denote the projections of $P_Y$ by $a,b$ and its arrow by $\tau:klb\Rightarrow fa$. By the $2$-morphism convention [def-trf-geometric-morphism], the inverse-image mate of $\tau$ at $u$ is $a^{-1}f^{-1}u\to b^{-1}l^{-1}k^{-1}u=0$. Its source is therefore initial by strictness of the initial set sheaf [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity]. Step 1 gives $a^{-1}u_X=0$. Apply the factorization clause of [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization] to the closed embedding $q$: there is $\bar a:P_Y\to(X_T)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with $q\bar a\simeq a$, unique compatibly with all $2$-morphisms.

source.place: Tags 08LY and 08M0: closed-complement factorization; agent specialization of XI 1.4, using the mate of the oriented arrow.

proof.text: The identity $fq=kf_T$ now rewrites $\tau$ as $klb\Rightarrow kf_T\bar a$. By [lem-trf-etale-closed-complement-sets], $k_*$ is fully faithful on sheaves of sets. Hence this transformation lifts uniquely to $\bar\tau:lb\Rightarrow f_T\bar a$: for every sheaf $H$ of $P_Y$, fullness gives the unique component $l_*b_*H\to f_{T,*}\bar a_*H$ whose image under $k_*$ is $\tau_H$; faithfulness makes these components natural. This explicitly checks the direct-image convention for $2$-morphisms. Apply [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] to $(\bar a,b,\bar\tau)$ to construct $w_Y:P_Y\to Q_Y$. Applying $k$ to $\bar\tau$ recovers exactly $\tau$, so $v_Yw_Y$ has the projections and oriented arrow of $1_{P_Y}$; uniqueness in that universal property gives $v_Yw_Y\simeq1_{P_Y}$.

source.place: XI Theorem 1.4 and §1.9; fullness of the closed etale embedding is Stacks 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward (1).

proof.text: Similarly, the first projection of $w_Yv_Y$ and the first projection of $Q_Y$ become the same morphism after composition with $q$. The factorization uniqueness, including $2$-morphisms, in [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization] identifies them; their second projections are both the projection to $Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$. After applying $k$, their structural arrows agree by the construction of $\bar\tau$. Faithfulness of $k_*$ [lem-trf-etale-closed-complement-sets] makes the arrows themselves agree. The uniqueness clause of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] gives $w_Yv_Y\simeq1_{Q_Y}$. Thus $v_Y$ is an equivalence for every $Y\to T$, without qcqs or point hypotheses. With $Y=T$ this is exactly $v:V_{f_T}\to E_T$. Its inverse image gives the claimed equivalence of set sheaves. Applying the equivalence to addition and scalar operations gives the module equivalence, with the constant coefficient ring identified by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image].

source.place: XI Theorem 1.4, uniqueness with projections and oriented arrow; direct closed-complement proof of the closed-immersion special case of Orgogozo 8.3.1.

proof.text: We record the precise compatibility needed on rectangles. For scheme maps $c:A\to X$ and $d:B\to Y$ over $S$ and $T$ respectively, form $A_T=A\times_ST$. There are induced morphisms $A_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to P_Y$ and $(A_T)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{T_{\mathrm{Et}}}B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to Q_Y$. Their square with $v_B$ (Steps 3–5 for $A,B$) and $v_Y$ commutes: both composites have first projection $c\,q_A$ followed by the source first projection, second projection $d$ followed by the source second projection, and oriented arrow obtained by applying $k$ to the source arrow. These are exactly the same triple of data in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], so its uniqueness gives the compatible isomorphism. For a composite of restrictions, the two resulting isomorphisms agree by that same uniqueness. This proves the required restriction compatibility for locally closed strata as well; no stratum is assumed to be etale or a representable object of the small etale site.

source.place: XI §1.9 functoriality and compatibility with composition, deduced from Theorem 1.4; applied also to immersions, not XI 1.10(b) etale localization.

proof.text: For any geometric morphism $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, inverse image preserves locally constant finite values. Here is the needed argument from the definition in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. A trivializing cover $(W_i\to1)$ pulls back to a cover $(h^{-1}W_i\to1)$: $h^{-1}$ preserves coproducts by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], and preserves epimorphisms because its adjunction turns cancellation after $h^{-1}e$ into cancellation after $e$. It preserves terminal objects and products by [def-trf-geometric-morphism], so it induces the corresponding slice pullbacks. A constant set sheaf of value $M$ is the sheaf coproduct of $M$ terminal sheaves (sheafify the constant presheaf), hence pulls back to the same constant set. For modules, [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] gives the identical finite module on each pulled-back slice. Thus local finite models pull back unchanged. If $h$ is an equivalence, apply its inverse to the same argument to obtain reflection as well. Finiteness is finiteness of the same set or module, without any invertibility hypothesis on its order.

source.place: Tag 093R, lemma-pullback-locally-constant (whose omitted proof is written here using the indicated constant and adjunction statements).

proof.text: The partition arguments use only Noetherian underlying spaces. Since $f$ is of finite presentation, it is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The closed-subset descending-chain condition on $S$ and $X$ is [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]; it is inherited by their closed subspaces $T$ and $X_T$ simply by regarding closed subsets of a closed subspace as closed subsets of the ambient space. Therefore every locally closed subset of any of these spaces is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Pulling back the strata of a finite partition gives a finite disjoint covering by locally closed subsets, since inverse images preserve open and closed subsets; the scheme strata are the actual fibre products. Conversely a stratum immersion into $X_T$ followed by $q$ is an immersion into $X$: factor it through an open of $X_T$, write that open as $X_T\cap O$ for an open $O$ of $X$, and view its closed part as closed in $O$.

source.place: Tag 005L, lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space; definition-stratification, with the displayed elementary pullback and composition of strata.

proof.text: Suppose $F$ on $E_T$ is constructible, witnessed by finite partitions $(X_\alpha)$ and $(T_\beta)$. Use the partition $X_\alpha\times_ST$ of $X_T$ and the same $T$-partition; Step 8 verifies the required locally closed constructible hypotheses. For each pair $(\alpha,\beta)$, Steps 3–5 applied to $A=X_\alpha$ and $Y=T_\beta$ give an equivalence from the target rectangle $((X_\alpha\times_ST)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{T_{\mathrm{Et}}}(T_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}})$ to the original $E_T$ rectangle. Step 6 identifies the restriction of $v^{-1}F$ with the inverse image of the restriction of $F$. Step 7 transfers the finite local models. This proves constructibility of $v^{-1}F$, for sets and for constant-$\Lambda$ modules, exactly by [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. Empty strata may be discarded; the same proof includes empty rectangles.

source.place: XI Theorem 1.4 and §1.9 applied to stratum immersions; finite rectangle criterion is the cited constructibility definition.

proof.text: Conversely, let a sheaf $G=v^{-1}F$ be constructible on $V_{f_T}$ with strata $A_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_T$ and $T_\beta\hookrightarrow T$. Regard the same schemes $A_\alpha$ as strata in $X$ and adjoin $X\setminus X_T$, using Step 8. Since $A_\alpha\to S$ factors through $T$, its base change $A_\alpha\times_ST\to A_\alpha$ is an isomorphism: locally a closed immersion is a quotient $R\to R/I$, and $B\otimes_R R/I=B/IB=B$ for an $R/I$-algebra $B$. Thus Steps 3–6 identify the corresponding $E_T$ rectangle with the $V_{f_T}$ rectangle, and Step 7 reflects the finite local models. The extra complement rectangle is degenerate: on it $a^{-1}f^{-1}u=1$ but the structural mate maps this to $0$, so [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] gives $1\simeq0$. Every sheaf there has the unique constant local model. These partitions therefore witness constructibility of $F$.

source.place: XI Theorem 1.4 and §1.9; agent reverse-partition argument, including the complement rectangle.

proof.text: Finally let $H$ be constructible on $V_f$, with partitions $(X_\alpha)$ and $(S_\beta)$. On $E_T$ use $(X_\alpha)$ and $T_\beta=T\times_SS_\beta$; these are finite constructible locally closed partitions by Step 8. From the maps $X_\alpha\to X_\alpha$, $T_\beta\to S_\beta$ and their maps to $S$, [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] constructs $h_{\alpha\beta}:(X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(T_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}\to (X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(S_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Its composite to $V_f$ is the rectangle map to $E_T$ followed by $r$: both have the same two projections and the structural arrow over $S$, so uniqueness identifies them, compatibly with further restrictions. Thus $(r^{-1}H)|_{\alpha\beta}\simeq h_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}(H|_{\alpha\beta})$. Step 7 transfers finite local constancy along this actual $h_{\alpha\beta}$; this proves the asserted preservation under $r^{-1}$ without using a comparison for the different map $v$.

source.place: XI §1.9 functoriality, checked for the actual map E_T to V_f; pullback of finite local models is Step 7 (Stacks 093R).

proof.text: For any closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow X$, apply the constructions above to $Z\to S$ and $Z_T=Z\times_ST$. Steps 1–7 were proved for arbitrary scheme morphisms and require only that $k$ and its base change be closed, the latter supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Steps 8–11 require only the Noetherian underlying spaces of source and bases; the closed subspaces $Z\subseteq X$ and $Z_T\subseteq Z$ have these by the descending-chain argument of Step 8. Thus no unverified finite-presentation hypothesis on $Z\to S$ is being used. The same partitions, complement, and canonical morphism calculations give all the assertions for $Z$. Identity and empty closed subschemes are included: the constructions reduce respectively to identity maps and degenerate topoi.

source.place: Closed-complement construction, Tags 08LY and 08M0; the preceding proof is independent of finite presentation except for the Noetherian partition check.

proof_origin.place: XI Theorem 1.4 and §1.9, together with Stacks 04CA, 08LY, 08M0 and 093R. Direct proof for closed immersions using the oriented arrow and complementary subtopoi; not a claim that XI 1.8 or 1.10 proves integral base change.
